openings.claim: Two ordinary removable, rubber-padded bolted strip clamps at opposing hatch edges might restrain sliding with modest, balanced pressure.
openings.delta: Replace unsupported hatch contact with two paired-strip clamps capturing the hatch edge and accessible rim underside. Drill only the supplied strips for outboard bolts. Alternate tightening instead of pressing one corner tightly. Loosen without removing nuts, withdraw both assemblies completely from the marked aperture, and retain assemblies and pads with the supplied cord.
openings.prediction: Relative to the supplied untreated-hatch rival, which slides 4 mm at 20 N, the clamps should reduce movement to within 1 mm of the mark through ten cycles, including the final right-contact card disturbance, while allowing reopening within 30 seconds. Balanced modest pressure might avoid the supplied opposite-corner lift; neither result is established.
openings.probe: First check that two 100 mm strip pairs can capture the rim without fixture alteration and that cord retention leaves the full opening clear. Fabricate within ninety minutes. Within twenty observation minutes, run ten numbered opening/closure/pull trials, with the final closure using the supplied right-contact 1 mm card. Record position before and after each 20 N pull, corner lift, opening time, and new visible seal tears; time reopening after the final trial. Stop and reject on seal damage. The supplied untreated observation is the rival reference, not a newly measured control.
assumptions: The unspecified rim profile permits underside access and outboard bolt clearance within the strip lengths.
The strips resist bending enough to clamp without permanently deforming the fixture.
Adequate friction is attainable without corner lift or seal damage; reject if increased tightening trades one failure for another.
Reject if the available cord cannot retain every loosened part outside the opening or manual release exceeds 30 seconds. No additional materials or relaxed constraints are assumed.

assessment: One conventional clamp incumbent, suitable only for a geometry-and-capacity probe. Rim access and achievable pressure remain indispensable unknowns; deployment and performance are unproven.
